execution.implementation: dated PubMed and PMC evidence, deterministic local five-method workflow map, and a genuine Rosalind task-chooser observation

observations: The exact-title PubMed query returned BayesSpace, Squidpy, SpotClean, Sprod, and SpatialExperiment records.
All five PMIDs resolved to PMC records; three were reported as PMC open access and two as manuscript or TDM records.
Rosalind Workbench returned its ready task chooser for the recorded case-specific invocation.
interpretation: The five papers provide complementary infrastructure, correction, denoising, spatial analysis, and region-aware method roles without defining one mandatory Visium workflow.
limitations: The named methods are a teaching selection, not a systematic review or benchmark ranking.
Workflow-role labels are title- and abstract-informed project classifications.
PMC manuscript or TDM records must not be described as CC BY open access.
The Rosalind call opened only the task chooser and did not execute a scientific job.

sources: NCBI Entrez E-Utilities PubMed ESearch, ESummary, and EFetch
provenance.note: The literature APIs supplied bibliographic and PMC observations; the local script produced the deterministic method map; the separate Rosalind observation preserves the exact task-chooser response and states that no scientific job ran.

reproduction: Repeat the retained exact-title PubMed query and compare the five PMIDs with outputs/query-verification.json.
Repeat identifier-specific PMC lookups before making current access or license statements.
Run python scripts/summarize.py from the case directory and compare outputs/results.json.
Inspect the preview against the retained five-method map.
Compare any new Rosalind launcher response with outputs/rosalind-open-observation.json without treating it as an analysis result.
